subject: Post-demo: Sherborne model-fit, prompt harvest & redaction guidance
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sherborne.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@sherborne.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Sherborne model-fit, prompt harvest & redaction guidance

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we can start a small eval focused on the three QA/knowledge tasks you showed: product Q&A, policy classification, and short-form summarization.

What we recommend / plan of attack:
- Recommended model variants to test (initial): Llama-3-70B (quantized 8-bit), Llama-3-13B (fp16) as a low-cost baseline, and a 70B/quantized fallback for latency-sensitive queries. We chose these based on your expected sequence lengths and multi-turn patterns.
- Benchmarks: I spun up a quick run on similar query mixes — see lightweight results here: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/llama3-70b-sherborne-run-2027-05-01 (will expand with Sherborne data).
- Prompt sets we need from you: 50–100 representative prompts (both happy-path and edge cases), 10–20 flagged PII/sensitive examples, and 25 negative/abusive examples you want the model to reject or classify differently.
- Redaction guidance: where possible, provide redaction rules (e.g., credit card numbers, national IDs), or mark fields that must never be sent to us (PHI/SSNs). If you prefer, we can redact on ingest and you can provide a redaction map. See attached sample spreadsheet (sherborne-prompt-samples.xlsx) with columns: prompt_text, expected_output_format, sensitivity_label, redaction_required (yes/no).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you fill the attached spreadsheet with 30–50 sample prompts by next Tuesday (2027-05-10)?
2) Send any regulatory constraints or retention policies we should know about (Data residency/SOC2/KMS keys).
3) If you have a procurement/technical contact for onboarding (for Dedicated or Private later), please loop them in.

Laura & Priyom from our side will prepare a short eval harness and a redaction checklist. We’ll propose a small 2-week pilot once we have the initial prompt set.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min follow-up if easier.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

We can supply the prompt samples. Attaching a first pass (customer-examples.txt) — pulled from support transcripts with obvious redactions applied. A few notes:

We’ll try to complete the spreadsheet with 40 prompts by next Monday (2027-05-09). If procurement needs to be looped in, that will likely be Maya (copied).

Hi Alex — Laura from Customer Success here. Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample dump — useful. A few practical notes from our side on redaction and evaluation so you can shape the spreadsheet quickly: 

Redaction & ingest guidance (recommended):
- Prefer client-side redaction where possible. If you cannot remove identifiers before upload, we can run redact-on-ingest with a redaction map you provide (we replace with <REDACTED:{TYPE}> tokens).
- Common things to mark in the sensitivity_label column: email_address, phone_number, customer_id, ssn, financial_account, free_text_pii.
- For multi-turn sessions: provide a session_id column and a turn_index column; that lets us reconstruct history without storing raw session metadata in the open.

Model-fit / eval plan (quick):
- Start with a 2k-sample bench drawn from your 40–50 prompts (augmented with negative cases) to validate quality/regression. We’ll run Llama-3-13B and Llama-3-70B-quantized to compare cost vs. quality.
- We’ll include BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics where applicable plus a small manual rubric for policy classification accuracy and false-positive rates (safety).
- If any prompt families are extremely latency-sensitive (<150ms target), flag them and we’ll prioritize a lower-latency serving profile.

Deliverables from our side after we get initial sheet:
1) Eval harness + instructions (notebook + scripts) — linkable so you can run locally if preferred.
2) A redaction checklist and sample replacements.
3) A one-page cost/quality tradeoff snapshot for the model variants we test.

If you want, Priyom and I can set up a 30-min workshop to align on the taxonomy and redaction rules next week.

—Laura
